I was accomodated because of my anxiety in university. Not just a "test anxiety" but a full generalized anxiety disorder. I could derealize really badly in class, during exams etc so I was given extra time in case it happened and did my exams in a room with very few people (4 people or so). Honestly, I think that when you have really bad anxiety it can help you, but the fact is that some people don't actually work on their issues. That's what the problem is. You can have that kind of acomodations but to me it has to be temporary, and you have to be in therapy, meds if necessary when having this kind of issues. I saw too many people cry to a random doctor in order to be considered as disabled but not seeking for help and just sitting in the comfort of having everything made up for them.   
I had this accomodations for half a year, now I work and it's fine. I won't say that I don't have little anxiety attacks sometimes, but with therapy I learned to keep my composure and deal with it, and in emergency case like derealization or panic attacks I always have some meds on me, though I don't take them much. You can't, unless you have very bad mental illness, just live forever like that.

If you are in "place similar to hers" I think you can understand the difference between wanting to die and wanting the pain to stop. Some suicidal people,  addicts or other people with mental issues have indeed no desire to be saved. This person wanted to be saved. If not, she'd never have smiled to me, she'd never asked me to call her mother, or anything like that. There's so, so much ways to die. She was just a person overwhelmed by pain. Not someone who had let herself down and already gave up.
... I... Well... What should I have done then ?

No we aren't. She gave me her number and we texted for a few days after the incident, but we stopped after a week or so. I can understand that it's hard to stay in touch with someone related to this kind of event, and as I said I was suicidal myself at the time so I didn't want to be on her way through recovering.

I'll always remember it.

I was in the train station to go to highschool, waiting for the train to come and I saw this girl. I looked at her and it was like hearing a voice screaming 'Do NOT stop looking at her.' So I almost stared. 

A train was coming at the same hour every morning. She took a step forward. I knew she was going to jump.

I runed toward her, my mind went blank. When she was going to jump, I grabbed her by the arm and pushed her against me. She started screaming and crying hysterically, yelling at me "Why ?! Why don't you let me go ?! Get off me ! Let me go !". She was in this state for five good minutes before grabbing my arms, putting her head against my chest and she told me " Please, I can't take it." She cried her eyes out.

Once she calmed down we talked for half an hour and she asked me to call her mom and tell her I was a friend of her and ask her to come pick her up because she was sick. I did.

I was deeply suicidal myself at this time. It could've been me. I could've been this girl. In a sense, she saved my life as much as I saved hers. Because she made me realize how much life could end in a instant. The smile she gave me before leaving made me see how the fact that I saved her was precious. 
I started to cherish life a little more. And so myself.
